abstract: The bidomain boundary element-cable method (Cable-BEM) couples the intracellular, membrane, and extracellular dynamics of multicellular neuron models using only the compartmental unknowns of cable models. However, its matrices are dense, and their storage and factorization scale as O(N2) and O(N3) for N unknowns, respectively. We compare four hierarchical matrix formats for compressing these matrices: hierarchically off-diagonal low-rank (HODLR), hierarchically semiseparable (HSS), H-matrices, and H2-matrices. For a layer 2/3 pyramidal neuron, the four formats use 2.7 to 6.1 times less memory than the dense solver. At a tolerance of 10-3, the maximum membrane potential errors are 8.5 mV for HSS, 0.47 mV for HODLR, and at most 10-3 mV for the H- and H2-matrices. For arrays of 9 to 225 parallel axons (1,827 to 45,675 unknowns), the maximum rank reaches 1,759 for HSS and 797 for HODLR, whereas it remains at or below 101 for the H- and H2-matrices. These results suggest that H- and H2-matrices scale more favorably than HODLR and HSS for networks of closely packed cells.
